Recovery checks used fixed absolute error limits that did not adapt to noisy-sensor baseline variability, producing post-clear false positives for tank1 in the noisy scenario.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Use early-prefix healthy statistics for each tank, add a learned tank1-to-tank2 coupling model for cascade decoupling, and make recovery thresholds baseline-adaptive. Further tuning of per-tank effort/error margins on additional scenarios may be needed.

proposed_change: Replace the whole-window quantile reference with an early-prefix median/error baseline. Lower absolute effort/error thresholds moderately and add relative deviation and sustained-fraction detectors. Estimate tank2's expected effort from tank1 using a linear regression on the healthy prefix, then flag tank2 only when its recent effort/error exceeds both the direct detector and the cascade-predicted value. Suppress cascade-induced tank2 alarms unless the excess is large or a long absolute tank2 signature is present. Make recovery adaptive to baseline error so noisy scenarios restore without false flags.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The current supervisor misses most faulted samples on both tanks because absolute/relative effort-error thresholds are too conservative, especially for moderately high pump effort or smaller error magnitudes. It uses a 0.20 quantile reference that can be contaminated by long faults. Tank 2 misses in both_faults are worsened by an all-or-nothing cascade suppression: whenever any tank1 evidence exists, tank2 is suppressed unless it hits very high spike/long-organized thresholds, so simultaneous tank2 faults are hidden. Recovery is also slower than needed, leaving non-zero restore gaps in tank1_fault_only and tank2_fault_only.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Monitor tank2 false-positive rate in tank1_fault_only after enabling the coupling-corrected tank2 detector. If tank2 is still flagged there, increase cascade_gain or tighten the cascade suppression threshold; if tank2 is missed in both_faults, lower dev2_eff threshold slightly.

proposed_change: Replace the fixed high absolute thresholds with lower, persistence-oriented thresholds. Use a lower 0.15 quantile reference to stay near healthy operation. For tank1, require high effort and error or sustained effort/error over 12-20 sample windows. For tank2, explicitly subtract a 0.70 fraction of tank1 deviation from tank2 deviation when tank1 looks active, so cascade disturbances do not look like local tank2 faults. A mild cascade suppression remains only when the corrected tank2 deviation is very small and absolute effort is not very high. Recovery now uses absolute healthy effort/error and restores in one step to eliminate final restore gaps.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The fixed 20th-percentile healthy reference is contaminated by long fault windows, so tank1/tank2 deviations shrink to zero and sustained faults are missed. Detection also relies too heavily on absolute pump-effort thresholds that are too high for the real fault magnitudes, and Tank2 is cascade-suppressed too aggressively in both_faults, causing most of the tank2 missed anomalies. In noisy_sensor_tank1_fault, tank1 false positives occur after true anomalies because recovery can be delayed, and tank2 is not flagged when it should be in both_faults.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Simulate the new adaptive baseline, lowered adaptive trigger thresholds, and cascade independence rule; if tank2 false positives appear in tank1_fault_only, tighten the tank2 independence requirement further (raise dev2 ratio or error margin). If both_faults tank2 missed anomalies remain, lower the tank2 independence bar slightly or add a tank1-setpoint-depressed conjunction.

proposed_change: Use a 5th percentile healthy reference instead of the 20th percentile so the baseline stays low even when a fault fills most of the window. Replace most fixed absolute effort thresholds with adaptive ref-relative triggers, and add an error-only trigger. Introduce a cascade independence test based on tank2's own strong evidence (spike, long organized signature, or high deviation with high error) before suppressing tank2; otherwise both_faults continues to hide tank2 anomalies. Keep restoration thresholds near original values to avoid restore gaps.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The supervisor was too conservative in marking anomalies, causing large missed_anomaly penalties in every fault scenario, especially both_faults where tank2's independent evidence was suppressed too aggressively by cascade logic. Recovery was also incremental, leaving restore_gap when faults cleared near episode end.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Re-evaluate with the modified detector; if tank2 false positives reappear in tank1_fault_only, tighten the tank2 spike/long thresholds or add relative magnitude gating while keeping the lower deviation-based early detection.

proposed_change: Lower deviation thresholds, add short-window sustained-effort/error evidence, add immediate last-sample checks, lower tank2 spike/long absolute limits to override cascade suppression earlier, and restore setpoints directly to nominal once a stable/recovered condition is satisfied.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The current supervisor estimates a healthy reference from the lower quantile of the entire telemetry window. Once a fault persists for a substantial fraction of the window the reference is dragged upward into the fault region, hiding the true deviation and producing large missed-anomaly counts in tank1_fault_only, both_faults, tank1_severe_persistent, and tank2_severe_persistent. Tank2's own detection thresholds are also slightly too conservative in tank2_fault_only. Cascade coupling suppresses tank2 on any upstream evidence, which helps tank1_fault_only but hides true tank2 faults in both_faults. Noisy sensor tank1_fault has excess tank1 false positives because recovery uses the contaminated reference and noise thresholds are not sufficiently robust.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Use an early-window median baseline for effort and error to avoid contamination, lower and make thresholds adaptive with absolute floors, require sustained evidence before flagging, strengthen tank2 independent-evidence tests before cascade suppression, and restore setpoints rapidly when the fault signature clears.

proposed_change: Replace the full-window quantile reference with a median baseline from the first 25 percent of the received telemetry. For each tank, detect anomalies using adaptive thresholds built on that baseline plus absolute floors. Tank2 is now only suppressed as a cascade effect when tank1 is clearly anomalous and tank2 lacks strong independent evidence (spike, long organized signature, or high sustained deviation). Recovery is based on returning to the early healthy baseline, and restoration toward nominal is faster.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The original detector requires both high pump effort and high absolute error before declaring an anomaly. In many fault cases the controller compensates enough to keep error modest, so the effort evidence alone never triggers a flag. Tank 2 detection is also too conservative, and cascade suppression is binary, so in both_faults the tank2 anomaly is masked even when tank2 has a genuine independent fault.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Add effort-only sustained-detection paths for both tanks, slightly lower absolute/relative thresholds where they were too high, and replace binary upstream cascade suppression with a coupling-ratio test that suppresses tank2 only when its deviation is consistent with upstream tank1 influence. Keep restoration conservative and verify no false positives in no-fault scenarios.

proposed_change: Introduce a frac_eff_high helper that measures high-effort persistence without requiring error. Lower tank1 absolute/spike thresholds and add an effort-only sustained condition; do the same for tank2 with softer absolute scales. For cascade handling, calculate expected tank2 deviation from tank1 deviation using a conservative coupling ratio plus margin, and only suppress tank2 if its deviation does not exceed that coupled expectation and it is not otherwise spiking. Recovery is tightened to avoid calling a compensated fault recovered.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The current supervisor's healthy reference is contaminated by persistent faults because it uses a 20% quantile over the entire telemetry window; once a fault occupies >80% of the window, the reference rises toward fault levels and relative deviation collapses. Detection thresholds are also too conservative for actual fault magnitudes, causing many missed anomaly timesteps on both tanks. Tank2's cascade suppression is too broad during simultaneous faults, and the restore step is too slow, leaving setpoints below nominal at episode end.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Use an early-window/low-quantile robust baseline, lower detection margins moderately, use median effort for robustness, strengthen tank2 independent-evidence escape from cascade suppression, and increase restore step to reduce restore gap.

proposed_change: Replace healthy reference with min(10% quantile of entire window, 20% quantile of first segment); lower effort/error thresholds moderately; use median recent effort; require strong independent tank2 evidence to avoid cascade suppression; restore setpoints at 1.0 per step instead of 0.8.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The current detector gates most anomaly signatures on both high pump effort AND high error. Compensated leaks settle into high pump effort with small error, so many tank1 and tank2 faults are missed. Tank2 is further suppressed whenever tank1 looks anomalous, so simultaneous tank2 faults are almost never flagged. Recovery and restoration are also based on a contaminated whole-window baseline, which can delay clearing or cause premature clearing.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Add effort-only persistent shift detection, use setpoint depression as memory, and require strong independent tank2 evidence before cascade suppression; tune recovery against a robust early/whole window baseline.

proposed_change: Add a median-based effort-only persistent shift detector for each tank, use active setpoint depression as hysteresis memory, and suppress tank2 only when tank1 is active and tank2 lacks an independent strong shift signature. Recovery now uses both early-window and whole-window baselines plus absolute healthy caps.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The largest score contributors are missed anomaly penalties in pure-tank and both-fault scenarios. The current supervisor clears anomalies too early once it has depressed a setpoint: pump effort falls because the target is lower, the recovery condition sees effort near the healthy reference, and the flag turns off while the fault is still present. Detection also still requires elevated effort and elevated error together in several branches, so compensated leaks with near-zero instantaneous error are missed. Cascade suppression is too broad and suppresses tank2 evidence even when tank2 has an independent moderate effort shift.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Keep anomaly flags latched while the corresponding setpoint is depressed, restore only after effort and error have been low for a sustained window, and clear only after the setpoint is near nominal and still low. Reduce cascade suppression to only weak tank2 evidence and let a depressed tank2 latch hold an independent tank2 diagnosis.

proposed_change: Introduce a depressed-setpoint latch that holds anomaly flags true until the setpoint has been restored and recent effort/error are low. Use median-based recent effort and add effort-only sustained-detection branches, while softening cascade suppression only for tank2 evidence that is not independently strong.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The current detector uses a full-window p20 reference and mean/abs-error gating. Full-window low quantile becomes elevated when a fault occupies most of the window, which hides severe persistent faults. Absolute effort thresholds are too high for moderate faults, and error requirements on sustained fractions miss compensated leaks. Tank2 cascade suppression is also too broad: tank2 is suppressed whenever upstream tank1 evidence exists unless tank2 has a very high spike or long absolute signature, so simultaneous tank2 faults are missed.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Use an early-window plus full-window low-percentile healthy reference, median recent effort and median absolute error, and error-free sustained effort fractions. Keep cascade suppression for upstream-only events but add a separate independent-tank2 evidence threshold that allows simultaneous tank2 faults to be flagged.

proposed_change: Replace the full-window-only healthy reference with min(full p20, early p35). Replace mean/mean-abs with median/median-abs. Use sustained effort fractions without an error requirement to catch compensated leaks. Lower moderate-fault thresholds while retaining a higher independent tank2 override for cascade cases.

failure_analysis.what_failed: Detection missed severe persistent faults because the healthy reference was a full-window 0.20 quantile, which rises toward the fault level when the window is mostly fault-filled. Compensated leaks were missed because several signals required a large instantaneous error alongside elevated pump effort. Tank2 cascade suppression hid simultaneous tank2 faults because the independent-override thresholds were too absolute and rarely triggered, so tank2 raw anomalies were always suppressed when tank1 was also active.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Use separate early-window baselines for each tank, allow effort-only detection for compensated leaks, and redefine strong independent tank2 evidence relative to tank2's early baseline with a high error-gated or large-deviation override so cascade suppression does not hide simultaneous faults.

proposed_change: Replace the full-window low-quantile reference with an early-window low quantile anchored to pre-fault operation. Use median recent effort instead of mean for robustness. Add effort-only absolute and sustained signals for both tanks. For tank2, redefine the independent-override condition to be based on relative deviation to tank2's early baseline plus error-gated absolute thresholds so upstream-only coupling is still suppressed while simultaneous tank2 faults can emerge.

failure_analysis.what_failed: Current cascade suppression rarely flags tank2 in both_faults because its independent-override thresholds are too high and tank2 raw detection is masked by tank1 coupling. At the same time, severe persistent faults are missed because the baseline reference rises when the window is fault-filled, and setpoint depression causes the detector to clear too early without a latch. Restoration steps are too aggressive, causing false positives and restore gaps.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Add a coupling-aware residual model for tank2 and cap baselines while implementing a depressed-setpoint latch; use smaller restore steps to cut restore gap.

proposed_change: The new supervisor anchors baselines with healthy absolute caps, uses a pre-fault linear regression to predict tank2 expected effort from tank1 effort, computes a tank2 residual over the recent window, and uses that residual both as part of raw tank2 detection and as an independent override for cascade suppression. It also treats a depressed setpoint as a latching condition, holding the anomaly flag until a longer healthy window is observed. Setpoint lowering and restoration steps are reduced and made more deliberate.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The current supervisor misses many anomalies, especially tank2 in both_faults and severe persistent scenarios, while producing false positives after fault clearance. Tank1 thresholds are too high for severe persistent faults, and tank2 detection is over-suppressed by cascade logic when tank1 is active. Restoration is too slow/incomplete after fault clearance, leaving setpoints depressed and adding false positives and restore gap.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Add a regression-based estimate of expected downstream pump effort from upstream effort to separate cascade coupling from independent tank2 faults. Use early-window 10th-percentile baselines plus shorter detection/recovery windows to reduce false positives after clearance. Lower detection thresholds moderately while relying on the residual signature to suppress tank2 coupling false positives. Speed restoration to one step when evidence is clean.

proposed_change: Improve baselines by using 10th percentile of early and full window. Fit early-window linear regression of tank2 effort on tank1 effort and use the residual as an independent tank2 signature. Shorten detection window k to 6 and recovery window h to 4. Lower tank1/tank2 absolute and deviation thresholds, and make sustained-fraction thresholds slightly more permissive. For tank2, use residual-based independent-override to avoid suppressing simultaneous faults while still suppressing upstream-only coupling. Restore setpoints in a single step when recovery conditions are met.

failure_analysis.what_failed: Current supervisor suppresses tank2 anomaly whenever tank1 is active unless tank2 meets a very high independent-threshold bar. This causes massive tank2 missed anomalies in the both_faults scenario. Detection thresholds for tank1 and tank2 are also too conservative for compensated or persistent leaks, causing missed anomalies in severe_persistent and fault_only scenarios. Recovery uses a relatively long 5-sample tail, which retains stale high-effort samples after physical fault clearance, causing false positives and restore_gap.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Use a regression-based cascade-coupling residual to distinguish downstream coupling from an independent tank2 fault, shorten recovery confirmation to the last 3 samples, and lower effort-shift detection thresholds while keeping absolute sanity caps to avoid treating a contaminated baseline as healthy.

proposed_change: Restructure tank2 suppression around an upstream-to-downstream pump-effort regression residual with a median-residual intercept. Add an independent-residual detector for tank2. Shorten detection/recovery windows to 6 and 3 samples respectively. Lower tank1 and tank2 absolute and deviation thresholds, and lower sustained-effort thresholds moderately. Keep the existing separate tank1 and tank2 physical scaling, but now tank2 can be flagged even while tank1 is active if its residual from the expected cascade coupling is persistently positive.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The current supervisor uses a window-min quantile baseline that becomes contaminated when a fault occupies most of the telemetry window, so severe persistent faults hide in deviation tests. It also misses moderate compensated leaks because Tank1/Tank2 absolute effort thresholds are too high and deviation thresholds require large excursions. Finally, tank2 is suppressed almost any time tank1 is active unless a very strong tank2 signature is present, which hides simultaneous tank2 faults in both_faults.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Anchor healthy baselines to the earliest few samples instead of full-window quantiles, use effort-only deviation thresholds plus absolute fallbacks, estimate tank2 coupling residual via Theil-Sen regression to separate cascade from a simultaneous fault, and latch anomaly flags while setpoints remain depressed.

proposed_change: Replace full-window quantile baselines with early-median/MAD robust baselines. Add lower effort deviation trigger thresholds and absolute fallback caps for severe start-of-window faults. Estimate downstream tank2 pump effort as a Theil-Sen regression on upstream tank1 effort over the first few samples, then use median residual to decide if tank2 has an independent anomaly or is only cascade-coupled. Latch anomaly flags while setpoints are depressed and restore only after a short healthy window.

failure_analysis.what_failed: Current detection thresholds were too conservative for moderate persistent tank1/tank2 faults, causing large missed-anomaly counts in severe and both-fault scenarios. Tank2 detection in both_faults was further suppressed by cascade logic unless tank2 had an extremely strong independent signature, so simultaneous moderate tank2 faults were hidden. Same-tank false positives and restore gaps remained because recovery used a fixed longer detection window and a slow restore step.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Tune the residual independent-override threshold and active-setpoint-dependent window switching on held-out scenario data; monitor upstream-only false positives after lowering tank2 raw thresholds.

proposed_change: Lower raw absolute/sustained effort thresholds for both tanks to catch moderate persistent faults, with tank-specific values. Add a robust Theil-Sen coupling regression from tank1 effort to tank2 effort and use the median recent residual as an independent tank2 fault signal, so simultaneous tank2 faults are no longer hidden by cascade suppression. Switch to a shorter recent-effort window when the active setpoint is depressed, which reduces post-fault false positives. failure_analysis.what_failed: The current supervisor misses severe persistent faults after an initial setpoint depression because low effort at a depressed setpoint is misinterpreted as recovery, clearing the anomaly flag too early.
